summary: Pre-trip vision post: a team of 7 undergrads will bike across the US running Learning Festivals with middle and high school students. It also announces a grant program for students anywhere in the US to fund their own projects.
learning_festival: Planned hands-on, mentor-led STEM festivals in towns across the US (e.g. model rockets, robots); no specific host or date in this post.
planning_notes: Pre-trip post (May 2015) announced a student grant program (funding and mentorship for community invention projects) open to students anywhere in the US; details are not in this post.

summary: Reblog of a post from the joyfuladventurer Tumblr; the entry has no text of its own.

First festival day at the Leonardo in Salt Lake City (post dated July 24, 2015): two 6-hour workshops for about 36 students. The Rockets workshop could not run because of a fire ban in Salt Lake City.
slept_at: John and Jill Kennedy's home (Harvard alums), Salt Lake City, UT (host)
learning_festival: Two 6-hour workshops at the Leonardo, Salt Lake City, about 36 students; the Rockets workshop was cancelled due to a fire ban. Another full-day festival was planned for the next day.
contacts: John and Jill Kennedy (Harvard alums, hosts), Salt Lake City, UT
planning_notes: Salt Lake City had a fire ban in late July 2015 that cancelled the Rockets (fire-based) workshop; check local fire restrictions before planning activities that need flame.
The Leonardo (Salt Lake City) hosted a two-day festival format: two 6-hour workshops on day one, about 36 students.

summary: Second-to-last festival day in Utah: another group of students and a successful festival. The team toured the Temple in Salt Lake City, then watched sunset at the Great Salt Lake; the next day's ride was Spanish Fork to Delta, UT.
learning_festival: Full-day festival with a new group of students; activities and location not described in this post (likely the Leonardo, Salt Lake City, from the previous post).
planning_notes: Salt Lake City Temple and Great Salt Lake (sunset, Black Rock viewpoint) were a good evening outing after a festival day.

summary: Two long Nevada days: 83 miles with no services, then 65 miles with nothing in between, with several mountain climbs, ending in Ely, NV. Car issues were the team's main worry.
planning_notes: Nevada has stretches of 65 to 83 miles with no towns or services between; carry enough food and water and plan stops before leaving the last town.
Nevada terrain is long flat basins with landmarks up to 20 miles away, then mountain passes; expect several climbs between Ely and Carson City.
The support car had issues on the Nevada stretch (Ely to Carson City); budget time for vehicle trouble.

summary: Hard day of about 85 miles with high heat, strong headwinds, and no towns to refill water after a late start. The next day was a 92-mile ride with no towns. The post does not name the location; it mentions grasshoppers in Kansas.
planning_notes: Late-summer heat and headwinds made an ~85-mile day with no water refills very hard; start early and check the wind forecast.
Carry extra water on 85-to-92-mile legs with no towns; the team had zero refill points for the next day's 92 miles.

summary: Went through Eureka, NV, and camped in Austin, NV, in a public park for a second night. They showered at the public pool. A 9 pm siren in Eureka turned out to be a curfew for under-18s.
slept_at: Public park, Austin NV (second night; showers at public pool)
planning_notes: Austin, NV: a public park worked as free camping, and the public pool provided showers.
Eureka, NV has a 9 pm siren for an under-18 curfew; it sounds like an emergency alarm, so warn riders in advance.

summary: Longest day, about 115 miles from Austin to Fallon, NV, including 15 miles across a salt flat on terrible pavement in extreme heat. They passed Middlegate (halfway) and skipped camping at Sand Mountain because it had no amenities.
planning_notes: Austin to Fallon NV (~115 miles) includes 15 miles across a salt flat with rough pavement; plan water and the heat for that section.
Middlegate, NV is about halfway between Austin and Fallon and works as a rest stop.
Sand Mountain, NV has no camping amenities (no water, no facilities); plan to continue to Fallon or carry supplies.

summary: Rode 60 miles to a Warmshowers host in Carson City, NV. A local person there had built tall bikes made from two stacked frames, and the team rode them.
contacts: Unnamed Warmshowers host, Carson City, NV
Unnamed local builder of stacked-frame tall bikes, Carson City, NV
planning_notes: Carson City, NV has a Warmshowers host the team used for a night.

summary: Rode from Carson City, NV to Krikwood, CA (spelled this way in the post), climbing Carson Pass south of Lake Tahoe. Drew's parents rode along for the day.
planning_notes: Carson Pass, south of Lake Tahoe, is a major climb on the Carson City to California leg.
